subject: Post-call: pilot slate checkpoints and performance links
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Walsh <emma@insightai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-27T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: pilot slate checkpoints and performance links

Hi Emma — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary of discovery:
- Primary use case: multi-turn customer-facing assistant that must preserve entity fidelity (order IDs, customer names) and perform concise summarization of support threads.
- Expected traffic profile: regional peak ~30 req/s, average sustained ~8–12 req/s; burst tolerance to 80 req/s for short windows.
- Latency target: p50 <= 120ms, p90 <= 300ms for short prompts (<= 512 tokens).
- Quality priorities: instruction-following, entity preservation, and minimal hallucination on pricing/product facts.

What I committed to share today:
- A curated pilot slate (attached) with recommended models and optics for your workload.
- Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS and latency percentiles) for the shortlisted models. See attached PDF and the bench link below.
- A starter prompt set for regressions and the initial evaluation harness (Drive link).

Immediate next steps / asks:
1) Review the attached pilot slate (insightai-pilot-slate.xlsx) and confirm which 2 models you want in the initial pilot window.
2) Share a small sample of representative prompts (or confirm we can use the provided sample prompt set).
3) If procurement needs us to pre-seed an SOW or a mutual action plan, loop in Sales Ops — we can draft a two-week pilot SOW that includes baseline acceptance criteria.

Benchmarks (quick highlights from the verified profiles):
- rw-opt-13B-q4 (recommended baseline): ~40 TPS (continuous), p50 80ms, p90 190ms, p99 380ms at 1k token context (batching enabled).
- meta-llama-2-13b-finetuned: ~28 TPS, p50 110ms, p90 260ms, p99 520ms (notes on quality: better instruction adherence post-finetune).
- rw-large-70B-fp16 (for quality headroom): ~6–8 TPS, p50 350ms, p90 720ms, p99 1.6s (recommended for a fallback tier where strict accuracy matters).

All full profiles + raw traces are attached (redwood-verified-profiles-202609.pdf) and available at: https://app.redwood.ai/bench/RDW-INS-2026-111

I'll stand up a short shared doc with the mutual action plan once you confirm which models you want to pilot. Proposed timeline: 2-week pilot (data ingest + 50k prompt run + quality/regression gates).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai


From: Emma Walsh <emma@insightai.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: pilot slate checkpoints and performance links

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we lock models:

1) For the rw-opt-13B-q4 numbers, are those with prefix KV-cache warmup and continuous batching enabled? We care about cold-start p99s for low-frequency customers.
2) Do you have an example prompt from the prompt set that targets entity preservation? We can share our anonymized examples but want to make sure the pilot covers NER-like edge cases.
3) On SLA: our procurement lead asked whether Redwood can commit to a 99.9% availability for the dedicated pilot pool. Is that feasible for a two-week pilot or does that require a contract amendment?

Also — can Marissa run the model-level expected cost delta for our traffic shape (we have a large tail of 1–2 req/day customers)?

If all looks good, we'll aim to confirm the two models by Friday and get Sales Ops to circulate the PO template.

Best,
Emma Walsh
Head of Product, InsightAI
emma@insightai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Walsh <emma@insightai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: pilot slate checkpoints and performance links

Hi Emma — quick answers inline + some concrete follow-ups. Attaching a compact cost/perf sheet in the same workbook for your traffic pattern.

1) rw-opt-13B-q4 profile details:
- Numbers shared were measured with continuous batching (target batch size 8) and KV cache at steady-state. Cold-start p99 (first request on a warmed container) is typically ~1.8–2.4x the steady-state p99 depending on sequence length — we include cold-start traces in the attached PDF. For low-frequency customers we recommend enabling a small warm pool (idle instances) as part of the pilot policy; this increases baseline cost ~6–9% but drops cold p99 to near steady-state.

2) Prompt set / entity preservation:
- Example prompt from the provided set:
  "Customer email: \"Hi, my order #A12-904 needs a refund\"\n   Task: Extract order id and intent, then draft a polite refund confirmation that echoes the order id exactly.\"
  Acceptance: order id must be verbatim and not normalized.
- Link to sample set: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-promptset (included in the workbook). We recommend running the full NER-ish subset (~8k prompts) as the first quality gate.

3) SLA for pilot pool:
- For a short two-week pilot we can provide a dedicated pool with 99.9% availability as an operational commitment (not a legal SLA). If procurement requires a contractual SLA, we can surface that in the SOW but it will need Legal review. We'll have Sales Ops draft the pilot SOW language.

Model recommendations (shortlist with observed perf / guidance):
- Primary pilot: rw-opt-13B-q4 — best cost/latency balance for your mixed workload. Expected continuous TPS: ~40 (1k token context), p50 80ms / p90 190ms / p99 380ms.
- Secondary pilot (higher accuracy headroom): meta-llama-2-13b-finetuned — better instruction following on conversational edits; expect ~28 TPS, p99 ~520ms.
- Fallback for high-accuracy: rw-large-70B-fp16 — use only for high-criticality paths (infrequent).

Quality regression guardrails we will include in the pilot package:
- Baseline reference set (the prompt set above) + automated daily runs producing: P@1 for NER extraction tasks, ROUGE-L for summarization, hallucination rate (labelled random sample).
- Regression alerts: daily drift >3% on key metrics triggers a flagged incident to your team + a rollback plan to the prior model snapshot.
- Prompt normalization rules: we include a small preprocessor to preserve order IDs and fixed tokens to reduce accidental normalizations.

Pilot mutual action items (proposed):
- InsightAI: provide representative prompt sample (anonymized) and a short list of 50 high-priority flows.
- Redwood: provision dedicated pilot pool, seed the evaluation harness, run 50k prompt bank across selected models, deliver daily quality dashboards.
- Sales Ops: draft pilot SOW / PO template.

Scheduling / timeline:
- If we confirm models by Fri (10/01), provisioning takes ~72 hours and the two-week evaluation begins on provisioning day.

Attached: insightai-pilot-slate.xlsx (tabs: model-slate, cost-estimates, prompt-map), redwood-verified-profiles-202609.pdf (raw traces + cold-start logs).

Happy to hop on a 20-min handoff with your engineering lead if that helps accelerate data handoff.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
